_comment: Hand-edited vocabulary that tokens.json cannot express: the words and glyphs that go with each state. Source of truth alongside tokens.json; build-tokens.js merges both into src/tokens.ts.

running.note: Animated pulse on the dot; static under prefers-reduced-motion.

waiting.note: The only status allowed in the title bar and sidebar counts.

succeeded.note: Chip scale only. Success never fills a row.

cancelled.note: Label is struck through. Neutral ramp: a cancel is not a fault.

blocked.note: An open dependency. Nothing went wrong and nobody is being asked.

held.note: Restrained by risk exposure or appetite.

stale.note: Dashed border. Shares the neutral ramp with cancelled: tell them apart by glyph, never hue.

empty.note: Nothing exists yet. The body says how to make the first one.

loading.note: No glyph on purpose: loading renders skeleton rows, and a symbol would compete with them.

error.note: Something failed to load. The body names what, the action retries it.

disconnected.note: Same glyph as the stale run status and the disconnected connection state, deliberately.

no-results.note: Things exist, this filter matched none. The action clears the filter, never the data.

attention.note: The waiting glyph, on purpose: the surface for the things waiting on a person carries the same shape the waiting status does. Nothing else in the rail is a diamond.

runs.note: Three stacked bars — a list of runs. Not a play triangle: the surface is what is happening and what happened, never a control that starts one.

plan.note: An outlined hexagon — a node in the dependency graph the surface draws.

workflows.note: A fork: a graph that branches, which is what a workflow is. Its own surface since the editor (#181), so a workflow is reachable from the rail rather than only by link or from a run.

agents.note: A ring around a filled centre: one who is doing the work. Solid ring, so it never reads as the half-filled running glyph.

config.note: Radial, in the place a cog would sit: U+2699 is in no OFL face ORCA bundles, so a cog here would be the OS's drawing on every platform.

commandKey.note: In keyboard hints, the command palette and menus.

danger.note: A destructive command in the palette, so the danger is a glyph as well as a colour (rule 4). The failed run's shape, because what it leads to is a run that stops.
